transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Head of ML, VelaBio), Ethan Park (CTO), Sara Gomez (SRE)

Summary:
Quick quarterly alignment to review current usage/cost signals, discuss capacity and reliability options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and kick off a pilot scope for a committed capacity pilot + perf benchmark. Customer emphasized strict latency SLO for their triage model, regulatory need for audit logs, and desire for deterministic per-token economics. Redwood AE/SE agreed to send pricing tiers and a test plan for perf/cost benchmarking.

Topics covered:
- Current usage profile & cost drivers
- Latency SLO for triage model and batch vs streaming tradeoffs
- Dedicated capacity / VPC options and security (SOC2, KMS)
- Benchmark plan: tests, metrics, staging access, and success criteria
- Rollout cadence: pilot -> canary -> full rollout

Action items called out in call (also in metadata): see action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll give about 45 to 60 minutes — we're hoping to leave with a clear pilot scope and a couple of action items. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Liam, our SE.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Hey team. Quick note, I'll be the technical lead for the benchmark design.
[00:16] Dr. Priya Nair: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we've been running two models in prod; the triage model gets most of the low-latency traffic and the longer-running summarization model is batched. Cost's been a surprise last quarter so we want to right-size.
[00:30] Ethan Park: Yep, and we have spikes during morning syncs — roughly 7-9am PST — those peaks are when our p99 blows out.
[00:38] Sara Gomez: Also want to call out compliance: SOC 2 Type II requirements, audit logs retention, and we use a customer-managed KMS for keys. We'll need details on KMS/HSM and VPC peering for the private option.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Great, all useful. Today we'll go over three sizing options: 1) Hosted with cost-optimized batching and prefix caching, 2) Dedicated reserved capacity with burst, and 3) Private (VPC) deployment for isolation. We'll map them to the triage model's latency SLO and your ops constraints.
[01:09] Liam O'Connor: Just to add, the runtime differences we usually surface: continuous batching can drop per-token cost by up to ~30% for low concurrency, but it adds tail latency. KV cache/prefix caching helps a lot on repeated prompts. Quantization may reduce memory/useful throughput but we need to validate model quality.
[01:32] Dr. Priya Nair: When you say 30% is that real-world? Our main fear is quality regression if quantize aggressively — accuracy for triage is top priority.
[01:43] Liam O'Connor: Totally agreed. The 30% is a rough median from similar customers; part of our pilot is validating generation quality vs quantization. We'll include A/B evals against your golden prompt set.
[01:55] Ethan Park: On the security side, how is KMS integrated in private vs hosted? Our legal team will want explicit HSM usage and key export controls.
[02:04] Maya Chen: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption in transit and at rest; Private deployments can be configured to use your HSM via networked KMS integrations. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts.
[02:17] Sara Gomez: Please include audit log retention windows and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Yes, logs can be exported; we'll include examples and retention options in the doc.

[02:35] Liam O'Connor: Alright, moving to performance: can someone share the p50/p90/p99 targets we should design against?
[02:42] Dr. Priya Nair: p50: 80-100ms, p90: 220ms, p99: 400-450ms for triage. The summarization model is fine with higher latency (p90 ~2s).
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: Okay that's tight for triage but doable with dedicated capacity or aggressive prefix caching + lighter batching. We'll propose a config that pins a small GPU pool for triage to keep deterministic latency.
[03:08] Ethan Park: Cost wise, we need an apples-to-apples per-100k-requests comparison across hosted vs dedicated. Also include a sensitivity analysis across average tokens per request.
[03:18] Maya Chen: We'll include a per-token model and a per-request runbook showing cost drivers. We'll attach a spreadsheet with scenarios — link provided in follow-up.

[03:30] Speaker 1: (mumbled) did you say the runtime supports automatic fallback?
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: Yes, smart routing and automated fallback to cheaper variants when capacity strained — good for graceful degradation. For mission-critical triage we usually recommend a pinned capacity priority to avoid fallback.
[03:44] Dr. Priya Nair: That makes sense. For the pilot we want deterministic behavior: no surprise model variant swap during business hours.
[03:51] Maya Chen: We'll include route policies in the plan.

[04:10] Sara Gomez: Regarding staging tests, what kind of access do you need? VPC peering or ephemeral keys? We prefer not to give long-lived creds.
[04:19] Liam O'Connor: Ephemeral creds for the benchmark runner are fine. For realistic networking tests we'll request staging VPC peering (read-only paths) and a test dataset small subset.
[04:30] Ethan Park: We'll try to get peering ready — need to coordinate with infra, may take a week.

[05:00] Maya Chen: Ok, pilot outline idea: 2-week perf validation in staging (latency, p99 stability, and cost per 100k up to 2M), followed by a 2-week canary in prod with throttled traffic. Success criteria: meet p90/p99 targets and show at least 15% cost improvement vs your current baseline without degrading output quality above the threshold you set.
[05:22] Dr. Priya Nair: That success criteria looks good. We'll supply the golden prompts and quality thresholds.

[05:45] Liam O'Connor: For quality we'll run automatic rouge/bertscore checks plus manual review on a sampled set. We'll share the evaluation harness.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Also note, rollout can include automatic rollback on quality regression or latency breach — we can wire in SLO-based automated fallback into the pipeline.

[06:12] Speaker 2: (interrupting) question on logging: are token-level logs included?
[06:16] Maya Chen: We can do token-level telemetry, but it's off by default for privacy. We can enable token-level cost attribution for troubleshooting only and route logs to your SIEM.

[06:30] Ethan Park: Pricing — do you have committed capacity discounts if we reserve a pool for triage?
[06:35] Maya Chen: Yes, committed reserved capacity for Dedicated gives the biggest delta. We'll model three tiers in the pricing doc: low, mid, high commit, and show the break-even point vs hosted.
[06:45] Dr. Priya Nair: And what about bursting? Some days we need double capacity for a short window.
[06:49] Liam O'Connor: Burst is supported; we recommend a small reserved base plus burst buffer. That keeps cost predictable while handling spikes. We'll show typical burst billing scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[07:05] Sara Gomez: On observability, can we get per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown? Our platform team needs traceability for billing and incident postmortems.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Console can surface per-route and per-model token breakdowns, traces, and error rates. We'll include screenshots in the follow-up deck.

[07:28] Dr. Priya Nair: One operational question — how long does a model rollback take if we detect a quality regression during canary?
[07:34] Liam O'Connor: Rollback is near-instant for routing-based rollouts (seconds to a minute to shift traffic), but if model reloading across GPU nodes is needed it can be longer; we'll plan to use routing controls first.

[07:50] Ethan Park: For the perf benchmark, what metrics should we provide so you can simulate?
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: 1) request rate histogram (1-min granularity) for last 30 days, 2) payload sizes and average tokens/request, 3) distribution of concurrent requests, and 4) golden prompt/sample dataset for evals.
[08:09] Dr. Priya Nair: We'll put that together.

[08:20] Maya Chen: Great. Next, quick risks: 1) quantization causing quality drift — mitigated via A/B evals, 2) VPC peering timeline — mitigated by starting with hosted or dedicated pilot, 3) billing surprises during burst — mitigated with cost alerts and burst limits.
[08:42] Speaker 3: (off mic) do you handle SSO/SAML for team access?
[08:45] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO with SAML/SCIM and RBAC are supported — we'll include the SSO setup doc.

[09:02] Liam O'Connor: Ok we'll recap pilot timeline: share pricing & test plan by 3/12, VelaBio shares data by 3/11, staging peering/access by 3/14, perf run 3/16-3/30, canary 4/1-4/14. Those dates are preliminary and adjustable.
[09:20] Dr. Priya Nair: Sounds reasonable.

[09:34] Maya Chen: Any other questions?
[09:37] Sara Gomez: One thing — retainer or SLA? For Dedicated we want an SLA. What's typical?
[09:43] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA packages; we'll outline SLA options and support tiers in the follow-up.

[09:55] Ethan Park: Regarding competitors, we've been evaluating LargeCloudAI and FastServe Labs; cost with LargeCloudAI is competitive but they lacked the unified rollout tools in our tests. ModelHostX had better latency but worse cost visibility.
[10:12] Maya Chen: Great context, helps us position the pilot.

[10:30] Liam O'Connor: Quick tech note: for the p99 target, we'll likely prototype a tiny dedicated pool (few GPUs) pinned to the triage route then measure KV cache hit rates; that will be the biggest lever for p99 reduction.
[10:46] Dr. Priya Nair: Ok that aligns with our ops thinking.

[11:00] (conversation continues with detailed clarifications, minor crosstalk and filler words; omitted here for brevity)

[42:10] Maya Chen: Wrapping up — to summarize: Redwood will send pricing, a dedicated vs hosted comparison, a benchmark plan and the follow-up deck + security whitepaper. VelaBio will provide traffic and golden prompts. We'll schedule the SE deep-dive for 3/16.
[42:35] Dr. Priya Nair: Confirmed.

[42:40] Ethan Park: One last ask — include examples of audit logs schema and an example trace for a request.
[42:45] Maya Chen: Will include both.

[52:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs and calendar invites.
[52:10] Meeting end.

Notes & links mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (will be shared), pilot plan deck (link to be sent), security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts, staging test harness (github repo link to be provided by Liam)

End of transcript.
